title: Stability of fixed life histories to perturbation by rare diapause: a packing bound for the family of strings of length T with k changes
author: David Steinsaltz; Shripad Tuljapurkar
work: Stability of fixed life histories to perturbation by rare diapause
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Lemma (source0.tex lines 1211--1220, source label L:packingbound): for positive integers T and k and radii above the critical value the packing number of the family of strings of length T with k changes is bounded by an explicit entropy-type expression, and a second bound holds for all radii; delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 1222--1252 (one adjacent proof environment of 31 lines that opens and closes inside the retained span). The proof is complete and closed inside the retained span and uses nothing outside the statement: it rescales the radius, partitions the index range into blocks of length k, maps each string to the sequence of positions at which it changes together with the changes themselves, verifies that this map is injective on a packing set, counts the possible images by a multinomial estimate, and applies the elementary binomial bound stated in the proof to obtain both displays. The lemma is a technical input to the article's comparison of diapause strategies, and its proof is a complete research-level counting argument. H2: a research-level combinatorial-probability lemma whose proof combines a block decomposition of the change pattern, an injective encoding of the packing set, multinomial counting and an entropy-type estimate; it is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises.
